extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of music, composers, music theorists, and philosophically-minded readers
extracted.subtask_description: Principled guidance and aesthetic criteria for composing, analyzing, and evaluating music (especially melody, harmony, rhythm, voice-leading, and the relation of music to words/drama) from a metaphysical/aesthetic perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of music over words
rubrics_metrics.description: Music is an independent art and does not stand in need of the words of the song or the action of an opera; the words are and remain for the music a foreign addition, of subordinate value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If words are incorporated, they must assume an entirely subordinate position and adapt completely to the music; music can produce its full effect without libretto. Composers should let the music lead and use words only as a secondary means to supply objects/motives of feelings. Anti-pattern: making music merely an accompaniment to insipid verses or letting the libretto dominate the composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music expresses the will directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Music acts directly upon the will (the feelings, passions, and emotions) and expresses the will itself rather than the Ideas or external objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compositions should aim to portray feelings and inner significance directly rather than represent external causes; instrumental music can and should express passions abstractly without narrative particularisation. Implication for evaluation: effectiveness judged by how directly and vividly music moves or represents affective states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice role and spacing (bass vs upper parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bass must be at a much greater distance below the three upper parts than they have between themselves; generally the bass should not approach nearer than within an octave of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended harmony (wide bass separation) is more powerful and beautiful than close harmony and produces a stronger effect; close harmony is only introduced because of limited instrument compass. Anti-pattern: crowding the bass into close proximity with upper voices which weakens the intended effect; exceptions allowed for instrumental limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody belongs to the high voice (soprano) by nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The musical ear follows by preference the highest note, not the loudest; the soprano, because of its rapid vibrations and great flexibility, has a natural right to deliver the melody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign principal melodic lines to soprano/upper voices for clarity and expressive suitability. Bass melody is unnatural and, if used, is achieved by counterpoint (an inverted bass) and properly requires a second fundamental bass accompaniment. Anti-pattern: giving melody to the bass without inversion/support, resulting in unnaturalness and reduced pure pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody composed of two elements: rhythmical and harmonious
rubrics_metrics.description: Melody consists of two elements, the rhythmical (quantitative, duration) and the harmonious (qualitative, pitch); both are necessary for complete melody though rhythm alone can sometimes produce melody (e.g., drum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composers must balance and integrate both elements; neglecting either reduces melodic completeness. In notation: rhythmical concerns vertical (perpendicular) placement, harmonious the horizontal; use both to craft melody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary coincidence of harmonic resolution and rhythmic accent
rubrics_metrics.description: For melody to arise, the attainment of harmonious intervals (e.g., tonic, dominant) and the return to the fundamental note must coincide with certain favourite points of the rhythm (accented beats).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that harmonic resting-points align with strong beats; misalignment (disunion) produces disquiet and prevents melodic satisfaction, while reconciliation produces pleasure. Example antipattern provided: harmonic arrival on a weak part of the bar followed by rhythmical accent on a dissonant scale degree causes disquiet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of dissonance and suspension to create longing and release
rubrics_metrics.description: Music consists of a constant succession of more or less disquieting (dissonant) chords and more or less satisfying (consonant) chords; the suspension (dissonance delaying final consonance) strengthens longing so the resolution provides greater satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce dissonances to avoid satiation produced by constant consonance, but resolve them again with proper preparation (e.g., the seventh on the dominant resolving to a consonant triad). Anti-pattern: a sequence of merely consonant chords that is wearisome and empty; unresolved dissonance that becomes merely painful rather than evocative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two fundamental harmonic types: dissonant seventh and consonant triad
rubrics_metrics.description: In the whole of music there are really only two fundamental chords: the dissonant chord of the seventh and the consonant triad, to which other occurring chords can be referred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose and analyze harmonic progressions in terms of contrast and preparation between these two types; use seventh chords to create tension and triads for relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major and minor keys as general affective types
rubrics_metrics.description: Music has two general keys, the major and the minor, which correspond to the two fundamental moods of the mind: serenity/healthiness and sadness/oppression respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose major for moods of serenity, minor for sadness or pain; recognition that minor is an unmistakable sign of pain and that cultural tendencies (e.g., northern nations) favor minor in certain repertoires. Use key selection deliberately to match affective content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm as the organizing principle (analogy to symmetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm is in time what symmetry is in space; it orders and holds music together through division into beats, bars, periods, parts, and movements—symmetrical distribution and repeated division bind a composition as symmetry binds architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ hierarchical rhythmic structure: beats → bars → periods (with internal rising/returning halves) → parts → movements. Typical forms: concerto/sonata often three movements, symphony four, mass five. Avoid incoherent rhythmic organization; use repetition and symmetry to round off musical wholes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Melody as alternating disunion and reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of melody consists in the constantly renewed disunion and reconciliation of the rhythmical and harmonious elements; this models the origination of new wishes and their satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose melodies that create temporary disunity between harmony and rhythm and then resolve them, using this alternation to evoke desire and fulfillment. The psychological effect (longing then relief) is central to melodic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical/arithmetical basis of consonance and the ear's preference
rubrics_metrics.description: All harmony depends on the coincidence of vibrations; so long as vibrations have a rational relation expressible in small numbers they blend as consonance; irrational relations produce dissonance. The musical ear follows higher notes (pitch/rapidity of vibrations) rather than loudness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose with awareness of simple vibration ratios to achieve consonance; rely on higher-pitched lines to carry melody even in strong accompaniments. Consider instrument limitations and the effects of equal temperament which introduce impurity when changing keys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modulation and role-change of scale degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: When the key-note is changed, the same note may figure as second, third, fourth, etc.; notes are analogous to actors who must assume different rôles while the person remains the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that modulation changes the functional role of notes and that equal temperament introduces unavoidable impurities; ensure that actors (instrument/voice timbres) suit their new rôles as far as possible.
